page: Microsoft Azure FX96-24ms_v2 is a specialized, memory-dense virtual machine within the FXmsv2 series, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture features a large 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction support including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Equipped with 1832.0 GB of system memory, the machine allocates an extraordinary 76.33 GB of RAM per vCPU, addressing scenarios that require vast memory pools paired with constrained compute counts.

Performance metrics reflect strong per-core efficiency driven by the high clock frequency and deep cache. Geekbench single-core tests register 2366.0, placing the processor in the top 10 percent of tested instances, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 34.65 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing demonstrates 118.92 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth across large 256 MB blocks, while multi-core compute tests yield a Geekbench score of 16770.0. In memory-bound operations, the instance delivered 38.78 million Redis SET operations per second and handled text generation on a 135M parameter language model at 314.26 tokens per second.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the compute-to-memory ratio and storage architecture. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring attached network or premium remote storage for disk I/O operations. Without local NVMe drives or integrated GPUs, overall input and output rely completely on network-attached systems. Cost efficiency is driven by licensing optimization: workloads constrained by per-core software license models benefit significantly from coupling massive memory density with a reduced physical core count.

The configuration is engineered specifically for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory caching grids, and memory-intensive analytics that do not need hundreds of concurrent CPU threads.
